Diospyra sat by the Sea of Reflection. The Crystal Scar was a quiet, subdued place. It was an ideal location for her to sort out her thoughts, close enough to Mar'dy that he could still be watched over, while far enough away from everything that there could be some peace and quiet.

Boy did Mar'dy require constant surveillance, somehow, while she was distracted, Mar'dy has managed to found a Floran city, picked up some unhealthy habits, and gotten himself completely marked from head to toe. In all honesty, the new look suited him, although it seemed a little overly extravagant.

Diospyra looked at her former body, frolicking amongst the crystal flowers by the shoreline. It filled her with a wistful sadness to see the sheer innocence that her form exhibited, the carefree joy with which she pranced through the crystal fields. The many bundles of plants that she carefully tended to and harvested, sometimes for practical reasons, sometimes for the aesthetics, reminded the spectre painfully of their past. Every day, the Saen reminded her more and more of who they once were, and she felt like Diospyra less and less.

It always came back to the same question, who exactly was Diospyra. If Diospyra was the sum of her experiences, then who was the Saen standing before her? If Diospyra was the physical form, then who was she?

That was a question that would be left to the ages, left to others to ask and answer. Diospyra, whoever she was, had no response. She did, however, have a solution. She rose, checking that nothing was left behind, taking the bundle of rosemary that was left on the ground.

Diospyra could only be reunited in her own body, perhaps she could never be the same again, but her memories could be restored. In order to restore Diospyra, the spectre had to remember what was forgotten. She had to have the strength to protect them both, and Mar'dy as well. She would have to gain some thorns.

*"Come now Diospyra, we must return, you wouldn't want our friends to get worried, would you?"* The spectre called out to the Saen across the Sea.

"Alright, I'll be right there Diospyra!"

*"No, that name belongs to you, little one."*

"What will your name be then?" The Saen shouted across the lake.

*"From now on, please call me Rose."*

*Rose for rosemary, rose for remembrance, rose, for its thorns. Please, let me be strong so you may be weak, solemn so you may be joyful. Let the name remind me of my duty, so I never lose sight again.*

With that thought, she cast one look back at the forest. The Forest of Reflection, a fitting name indeed.

A name should reflect a purpose, and she knew her purpose now. Rose, would be lost no longer.
